Mirela, I’m back! You told me you went to Machu Picchu. Well, now I’ve been there too.
How was it? Was it foggy when you arrived?
Very! We set off at five, and we were climbing the trail when the clouds came down. We couldn’t see a thing.
Oh no! And did the fog go away?
Yes, at about nine. I was standing at the viewpoint when the sun came out, and suddenly the whole city was there.
That’s the moment everybody waits for. Did you feel the altitude?
A little. I was out of breath on every staircase. And while I was taking a photo of the ruins, a llama walked right in front of me.
That’s the best photo of the trip. It sounds unforgettable.
It was foggy, so we couldn't see anything.
We set off very early, before sunrise.
The view from the top was unforgettable.

Good morning, everyone. Let me tell you a little about this place. The Inca people built this city in the fifteenth century, about five hundred years ago. For a long time, the world didn't know about it. It was hidden in the mountains, and only local farmers knew it was here. Then, in 1911, an American explorer was traveling through the region when a farmer showed him the way. He took photos, and soon the whole world was talking about the lost city of the Incas. Today it's the most famous landmark in Peru. Now, please stay on the trail, and watch your step.

I'm pretty fit. I run three times a week, so I wasn't worried about the altitude. Big mistake. On my first day in Cusco, I was walking up the stairs of my hotel when I suddenly felt dizzy. I had a headache, and I was completely out of breath. While I was sitting on the stairs, a woman from the hotel came and gave me a cup of coca tea. She told me to rest for the whole afternoon. I did, and the next day I was fine. My advice: on the first day, take it easy. The mountains aren't going anywhere.

There are two ways to get to Machu Picchu. You can take the train, or you can walk the trail for four days. I chose the trail. It was hard. On the third day, it was raining all day, and we were walking in the mud for hours. At night, I was so tired that I fell asleep during dinner. But on the last morning, we set off at four, and we were walking through the Sun Gate when the sun came up over the ruins. Unforgettable. My parents took the train the same week. They loved it too. They were drinking coffee and looking at the river the whole time.
